rows.title: Hutchins’ year in review: The news behind the news in Colorado’s media world in 2022
rows.standfirst: Colorado newspapers turned into nonprofits, researchers mapped news in each county, and more

rows.title: State lawmakers wrestle with how to issue future TABOR refunds after Colorado voters slash income tax rate
rows.standfirst: The legislature may choose to keep refunds tied to Coloradans’ income levels, or they could repeat what they did in 2022: issue flat sums

rows.title: After years of profits, many Colorado hospitals are facing a downturn
rows.standfirst: Investment losses and higher staffing and supply costs are all contributing, but one expert cautions to look at the long-term picture

rows.title: Could Colorado communities get to 100% renewable energy faster than utility companies? Lawmakers may provide the tool.
rows.standfirst: Community choice electric, or CCE, is a concept pioneered in 1999. Xcel Energy says it’s a solution to a carbon problem that is already on its way to being solved.

rows.title: 4 Colorado electric co-ops want repayment after Xcel Energy allegedly mishandled gas supply during a deep freeze
rows.standfirst: Xcel appears to have directed its own natural gas supply to meet reserve requirements rather than generate power during 2021 storm. “It’s like someone is knocking on your door to pay a credit card bill and you are putting the money in savings.”

rows.title: Here are all the new EV and e-bike tax credits heading Colorado’s way
rows.standfirst: Denver relaunches popular e-bike vouchers and Polis proposes major new car-buying credits to promote clean electrification.

rows.title: Deadline nears for correcting Colorado locations with terrible broadband service
rows.standfirst: Accuracy in the new national broadband map is key in determining how much of the $42.5 billion in broadband infrastructure funds Colorado could receive.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado business leaders are pessimistic about 2023. Should they be?
rows.standfirst: A survey of Colorado business leaders said they’re still pessimistic about the new year, with more than half believing that the U.S. will enter a recession within the next six month.

rows.title: Unpaid wages, injuries: The dark side of a celebrated Colorado mushroom farm known for helping migrants
rows.standfirst: Dozens of interviews show hidden perils for immigrants working at Colorado Mushroom Farm, which sold produce at Whole Foods and King Soopers before going bankrupt.

rows.title: Colorado governor calls for more property tax relief as long-term solution to rising tax bills remains elusive
rows.standfirst: If approved, it will mark the third time in as many years state lawmakers slap a Band-Aid on a problem that has big ramifications for schools and local governments.

rows.title: Avian flu wreaks more havoc in Colorado egg layers and wild birds
rows.standfirst: Worst-ever outbreak leads to slaughter of 6 million-plus chickens and has killed enough eagles and other raptors to raise wildlife fears.

rows.title: 2DRTY4CO: DMV releases list of more than 140 rejected Colorado license plates
rows.standfirst: Personalized license plate requests — which have been rejected for being offensive, vulgar and rude — are weeded out by an automatic flagging system

rows.title: Aurora landlord who hired armed guards to evict motel residents faces a second lawsuit
rows.standfirst: The VareCo settled with three plaintiffs involved in the first class-action lawsuit. Now 18 more residents are suing the property manager for similar claims.

rows.title: Yurt operator at a Colorado state park disappeared with guests’ money
rows.standfirst: CPW revoked the contract for Never Summer Nordic Yurts in the fall and now says the company must remove 10 yurts and cabins by the end of June

rows.title: Denver bought one-way bus tickets for 1,900 migrants. Here’s where they were going.
rows.standfirst: Some of the top destinations were Chicago, New York City, Atlanta, Miami and Dallas

rows.title: What’s Working: How Colorado’s high egg and energy prices mesh with its slowing inflation
rows.standfirst: The Denver metro area’s 8% annual inflation rate in 2022 was the highest in decades. Plus: Readers share their economic outlook, personal savings is in decline, and more!

rows.title: Colorado ski areas open day cares to attract high country workers in child care desert
rows.standfirst: Steamboat Resort and Breckenridge Resort opened child care centers for the kids of their employees this season. In Aspen, the resort is helping pay for new child care center slots in the community.

rows.title: Colorado retirement plan launches for those without one, including self-employed, gig and farm workers
rows.standfirst: The Colorado SecureSavings plan sets up a Roth IRA with automatic paycheck deductions. So far, 129 of an estimated 115,000 businesses that are likely required to enroll have done so.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s unemployment rate dropped, but so did the number of people in the workforce
rows.standfirst: Businesses added jobs, but more people left the job market in December. Plus: Colorado leads highest increase in gas prices, readers share annoying inflation interactions, and more!

rows.title: Why the ground under Colorado solar panels is ripe for growing food
rows.standfirst: A Republican lawmaker has joined the previously Democrat-only push for solar agriculture, or agrivoltaics, priming Colorado to become a national leader

rows.title: K.P. Kauffman asks for more time to clean up troubled oil and gas wells. Colorado regulators are out of patience.
rows.standfirst: KPK says it will be in better financial condition if it sells northeastern Colorado wells to a company proposing to use them for a carbon capture project.

rows.title: Colorado may end the ultimate age-discriminating work question: How old are you?
rows.standfirst: It’s legal to ask job applicants their age, high school graduation date or birth date. Senate Bill 58 would put an end to answering those awkward questions.

rows.title: As gas car sales drop, how many electric vehicles did Colorado buy in 2022? A lot.
rows.standfirst: Overall car market is down, but the state is adopting cleaner electrics and hybrids at a pace that makes state leaders happy

rows.title: Programs offering universal basic income — or direct cash with no strings attached — are increasing across Colorado
rows.standfirst: Dozens of Colorado nonprofits are funding direct cash programs they say have led to economic stability for individuals and families.

rows.title: Carman: Family’s quest to help undocumented Coloradans began long ago, when Mexico saved 6 Jewish refugees
rows.standfirst: Left Behind Workers Fund, co-created by Mark Newhouse, helped distribute $38 million to people who could not legally collect government aid after the pandemic left them jobless.

rows.title: Colorado joins 7 other states, Justice Department in suing Google over its digital advertising dominance
rows.standfirst: The government alleged in the complaint that Google is looking to “neutralize or eliminate” rivals in the online ad marketplace through acquisitions and to force advertisers to use its products

rows.title: Colorado utility bills are high because of two things state regulators can’t control: Weather and gas prices
rows.standfirst: State utilities regulators called a hearing to discuss how — and if they can — lessen impacts of frigid weather and pressure in the natural gas market

rows.title: Heat pumps are having a moment in Colorado, but do they really work in the bitter cold? Yes.
rows.standfirst: Developed in 1857, tech improvements are making heat pumps a viable element in the contemporary transition to cleaner, more energy efficient homes.

rows.title: Xcel building massive battery to store clean energy at Pueblo’s Comanche complex
rows.standfirst: Power company hailed for 10 MW storage site the size of a football field that can hold days of electricity from wind and solar to bolster the Colorado grid

rows.title: Massive rock slide halts operations at Glenwood Springs quarry. Mine opponents call for shut-down, investigation.
rows.standfirst: Federal and state mining regulators are investigating the rock slide at the quarry owned by Rocky Mountain Industrials, which is proposing a controversial mine expansion

rows.title: What’s Working: Get ready for Colorado’s wage transparency law, part 2
rows.standfirst: The state’s Equal Pay for Equal Work law influenced new laws in other states. But it wasn’t perfect, apparently. Plus: Wage transparency violators fined, other labor bills and more.

rows.title: How to make the right ethical decisions when recycling and reusing as Colorado pushes for clean energy
rows.standfirst: We asked recycling and reuse experts to take on a reader’s dilemma about retiring perfectly good fossil fuel-powered machinery.

rows.title: Vail Resorts sees uptick in skier traffic over last year’s record showing — but not in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The company’s five resorts here are seeing mellow traffic despite well-above-average snowpacks
